chunks: They leapt upon me as the camels leap upon each other on their arrival for drinking water,
having been let loose after unfastening of their four legs till I thought they would either kill me or kill one another in front of me.
I thought over this matter in and out to the extent that it prevented me from sleeping.
But I found no way except to fight them or else to reject whatever has been brought by Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family),
I found that to face war was easier for me than to face the retribution, and the hardships of this world were easier than the hardships of the next world.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali describe the chaos during the swearing of allegiance in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) vividly depicts the chaotic rush of people during the swearing of allegiance, comparing their intensity to unfastened camels at a watering hole. He reflects on his dilemma between fighting the people or rejecting the prophetic message, ultimately choosing the former as the lesser of two evils to avoid the punishment of the Hereafter. This passage highlights the historical context of his reluctant acceptance of leadership to preserve the unity of the Muslim community and the integrity of Islam's message.
